Hit & Run (2021) is Netflix’s tense, high-stakes political thriller and crime-drama series created by Lior Raz, Avi Issacharoff, and Dawn Prestwich, exploring international espionage, betrayal, and deep-seated state corruption.

The Setup: Segev Azulai (Lior Raz), a former elite Israeli soldier turned Tel Aviv tour guide, sees his world violently shattered when his American-born dancer wife, Danielle, is killed in a mysterious hit-and-run accident on the eve of her big New York audition. As Segev desperately investigates the truth behind her death, he uncovers a labyrinth of deceit involving high-ranking intelligence agencies, corporate espionage, and a double life that Danielle kept entirely hidden from him. Pursued across borders from Tel Aviv to New York, Segev must weaponize his former military skills to uncover who targeted his family and why.

The Systemic Breakdown:

State Espionage and Collateral Damage: The narrative deconstructs how intelligence agencies and international security apparatuses routinely treat ordinary civilian lives as disposable collateral in covert geopolitical power struggles.

The Illusion of Security: It highlights how absolute surveillance states and elite military operations fail to protect individuals, instead generating environments where paranoia and betrayal thrive.

Institutional Cover-Ups: The series exposes how powerful organizations use systemic secrecy, bureaucratic stonewalling, and bureaucratic impunity to bury state-sponsored crimes.

The Bottom Line: Hit & Run is a relentless thriller that demonstrates how deeply personal grief can collide with global geopolitical corruption, leaving ordinary people trapped in a game they never chose to play.

When national security apparatuses operate above the law and treat human lives as expendable assets, can an individual ever find true justice, or is the entire system rigged to bury the truth?
